2026-09-17.eventTitle: Birth of Agostinho Neto, Angola's founding president
2026-09-17.infoText: Agostinho Neto, the founding president of Angola, was born on September 17, 1922. He led the Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola during the long struggle against Portuguese colonial rule and became the country's first president when it gained independence in 1975. Angola marks his birthday each year as National Heroes' Day, honoring him as the father of the modern nation.

2026-09-18.infoText: On September 18, 1980, Arnaldo Tamayo Méndez launched into space aboard the Soviet Soyuz 38 spacecraft. He became the first Cuban, the first Latin American, and the first person of African descent to travel to space. His flight was part of the Soviet Union's Intercosmos program, which invited guest cosmonauts from allied nations to join its missions.

2026-09-19.eventTitle: St Kitts and Nevis's Independence Day
2026-09-19.infoText: St Kitts and Nevis became an independent country on September 19, 1983, when it gained full sovereignty from the United Kingdom. The twin island nation in the Caribbean is the smallest sovereign state in the Americas by both land area and population. Independence Day is celebrated each year with parades, music, and cultural festivities across both islands.

2026-09-20.eventTitle: Capture of Rome completes Italian unification
2026-09-20.infoText: On September 20, 1870, Italian troops broke through the walls of Rome and took the city, ending centuries of papal rule over the region. This event completed the unification of Italy into a single kingdom after decades of separate states and foreign rule. The anniversary is still remembered in Italy as the day the country's modern borders were completed, and many streets are named Via XX Settembre in its honor.

2026-09-21.infoText: Belize became an independent country on September 21, 1981, ending its status as a British colony formerly known as British Honduras. It was the last country on the mainland of the Americas to gain independence from a European power. Each year Belizeans celebrate with parades, music, and festivities that often begin the night before with a lively street carnival.

2026-09-22.infoText: Ukraine marks the Day of Partisan Glory every September 22, honoring the resistance fighters who fought behind enemy lines during the Second World War. The holiday recalls the formation of the first Ukrainian partisan detachments in 1941, shortly after Nazi Germany invaded the Soviet Union. It was officially established as a day of remembrance in 2001 and today also honors modern Ukrainian volunteers defending their homeland.

2026-09-23.infoText: On September 23, 1868, a group of Puerto Rican revolutionaries launched an armed uprising against Spanish colonial rule in the mountain town of Lares. Spanish forces put down the rebellion within days, but the Grito de Lares became a lasting symbol of Puerto Rican identity and the desire for self government. The date is still commemorated every year across the island with speeches, parades, and cultural events.

2026-09-24.infoText: National Punctuation Day is celebrated in the United States every September 24, dedicated to the correct use of commas, semicolons, apostrophes, and other punctuation marks. It was created in 2004 by journalist Jeff Rubin, who wanted to draw playful attention to a serious writing skill. Fans of the quirky holiday mark it with punctuation themed treats and contests for spotting badly punctuated signs.

2026-09-25.infoText: Mozambique observes Armed Forces Day every September 25, marking the start of its armed struggle for independence from Portugal in 1964. On that date, fighters from the Mozambique Liberation Front, known as Frelimo, launched their first attack on a Portuguese administrative post in the northern Cabo Delgado region. The guerrilla war that followed lasted a decade and eventually led to Mozambique's independence in 1975.

2026-09-26.infoText: Jordan is a kingdom in the Middle East, with its capital and largest city, Amman, sitting on hills overlooking the Jordan River valley. The country is home to Petra, an ancient city carved into rose colored cliffs by the Nabataeans more than two thousand years ago. Jordan has been ruled as a monarchy by the Hashemite royal family since it gained independence from Britain in 1946.

2026-09-27.infoText: Turkmenistan declared its independence from the Soviet Union on September 27, 1991, following a national referendum. The Central Asian nation, much of which is covered by the Karakum Desert, marks the date each year with large military parades and cultural celebrations in the capital, Ashgabat. Independence Day is one of the most important holidays on the Turkmen calendar.
